title: Shortness of breath at 34 weeks of pregnancy
presenting_complaint: Sudden shortness of breath and right-sided pleuritic chest pain that began 3 hours ago while she was walking upstairs, at 34 weeks of pregnancy. No haemoptysis, no fever.
history: G2P1, 34 weeks pregnant. The pregnancy has been uncomplicated. She flew back from a family visit (9-hour flight) five days ago. She denies calf pain or leg swelling. No previous VTE, no known thrombophilia. Non-smoker. Takes only prenatal vitamins.

findings.name: General appearance
findings.value: Alert, anxious, speaking in short sentences

findings.name: Leg examination
findings.value: No oedema, calves soft and non-tender

findings.name: ECG
findings.value: Sinus tachycardia 118/min, S1Q3T3 pattern, T-wave inversion V1–V3

findings.name: Arterial blood gas on room air
D-dimer
findings.value: 3.8 mg/L (of limited value in the third trimester)

findings.name: Bedside echocardiography
findings.value: Dilated right ventricle, normal LV function

findings.name: CTPA with abdominal shielding
findings.value: Filling defects in the right lower lobe segmental arteries

diagnosis_options.label: Pulmonary embolism
diagnosis_options.explanation: Sudden dyspnoea and pleuritic chest pain at 34 weeks after a 9-hour flight, with tachycardia, hypoxaemia, S1Q3T3 with T-wave inversion V1–V3, dilated right ventricle and CTPA filling defects in the right lower lobe segmental arteries.

diagnosis_options.label: Peripartum cardiomyopathy
diagnosis_options.explanation: Differential mentioned in the text; no signs of heart failure, LV function normal on echo, and CTPA confirms emboli.

diagnosis_options.label: Community-acquired pneumonia
diagnosis_options.explanation: Differential mentioned in the text; no fever, chest clear on auscultation, and CTPA shows embolic filling defects rather than consolidation.

diagnosis_options.label: Amniotic fluid embolism
diagnosis_options.explanation: Differential mentioned in the text; typically presents with sudden collapse, hypotension and coagulopathy during labour or delivery, not with isolated pleuritic pain and preserved haemodynamics.

diagnosis_options.label: Spontaneous pneumothorax
diagnosis_options.explanation: Differential mentioned in the text; chest is clear on auscultation and CTPA shows no pneumothorax.

diagnosis_options.label: Acute coronary syndrome
diagnosis_options.explanation: Plausible differential for chest pain and dyspnoea, but troponin is normal and the CTPA demonstrates pulmonary emboli.

management_options.label: Therapeutic low-molecular-weight heparin, weight-adjusted
management_options.explanation: Essential; LMWH is the anticoagulant of choice in pregnancy and should be started empirically for high clinical probability of pulmonary embolism.

management_options.label: Oxygen to keep SpO2 at 94% or above
management_options.explanation: Essential; the patient is hypoxaemic (SpO2 91% on room air, pO2 62 mmHg) and fetal oxygenation depends on maternal oxygenation.

management_options.label: Urgent obstetric review and fetal monitoring
management_options.explanation: Essential in a third-trimester pregnancy with a significant maternal event and hypoxaemia.

management_options.label: Systemic thrombolysis
management_options.explanation: Not indicated in a haemodynamically stable patient; harmful.
